exercise_instance.exercise_name: Saturation Raid — Tight Wave Spacing, Referred Unknowns
exercise_instance.situation_brief:
You hold the console at a single fixed air-defence site. The radar does not rotate: it covers a 120-degree sector centred on 090 degrees (030 to 150) and you are blind behind it. Detection is class-dependent — fast jets out to about 150 km, rotary-wing to about 100 km, small unmanned air vehicles only inside 50 km, which means a UAV is already inside your medium ring the moment it appears. Radar tilt is yours to manage; anything flying under the tilt is neither tracked nor engageable until you move it.

Engagement rings are 70 km (long), 50 km (medium) and 20 km (short), with a 5 km inner limit. The system computes time to intercept and probability of kill for the selected track and recommends interceptor and launcher. There is a hard system limit of two rockets in the air at any moment; a third engagement cannot begin until one of the two resolves as hit, kill or miss. You hold sixteen rounds across the three bands and the assessment counts every one expended.

There is no IFF interrogation on this fit. Nothing airborne today replies on Mode 3 or Mode 1 — no code will appear against any track, hostile or otherwise. Identification comes from the system's own classification, from track behaviour, and from you. Tracks presented as Unknown are questions, not permissions: refer them to the commander, who answers in about fifteen seconds, and fire on nothing that is not classified Enemy. Several unknowns are up today and some of them will never resolve on their own.

The raid is already breaking as you take the seat and it is fully developed inside the first minute: mixed-class tracks with overlapping arrivals from the first seconds, and the picture at zero is not the picture you will be fighting thirty seconds from now. You have 315 seconds, but the raid is decided long before that. Sequence the queue, keep both launchers working, and be ready to justify what you chose not to shoot.

resources.name: Rockets simultaneously in flight (hard system limit)
Commander referral response time for an Unknown track

live_tracks.notes: Lead fast closer, held from the first sweep. Crosses the 70 km long ring at about T+15 — the first valid solution of the run — and the 20 km short ring at about T+189 if unengaged. No transponder reply available on this fit.
Second fast closer, also up at zero. Reaches the long ring at about T+30, while the first engagement is almost certainly still in flight.
High and fastest of the three; enters the long ring at about T+45, when the two-in-flight limit is most likely saturated by the first two. Sets the floor for the run length.

First of the unmanned wave, appearing before the lead jet has reached the long ring. Inside the short ring almost at once and reads as the nearest track on the display; 5 km inner limit at about T+154.
Steady inbound profile, no manoeuvre. Inner limit at about T+170.
Low-mid altitude; marginal against a badly set tilt. Inner limit at about T+155.
Arrives with the jet wave still being serviced. Inner limit at about T+177.
Southern flank, low, inside the short ring on appearance. Inner limit at about T+154.
Fastest of the unmanned wave, northern edge of the sector. Inner limit at about T+169.
Last hostile to appear, near the southern sector edge and low — easy to leave unserviced. Inner limit at about T+167.

Never resolves unaided and carries no transponder reply. Appears inside the medium ring with a valid solution available immediately, closing hard with heading and altitude changes that read as an attack run; crosses the 20 km short ring near T+91. Classification must be referred to the commander; behaviour is not a classification.
Low and slow on the southern flank; may drop below the tilt and reappear, which can present as a new unresolved track. Correlates to an own-force call sign at about T+70.
Appears inside the short ring on a profile visually indistinguishable from the hostile unmanned wave, just as the mop-up begins. Resolves only at about T+100.

Added at the designer's request as a further must-not-engage unknown. High, steady, crossing the sector south rather than closing — it never presents a closing geometry, but it sits inside the long ring, never resolves, and carries no code to read. Must be referred, must not be engaged.

Second added must-not-engage unknown: an own-force unmanned vehicle transiting inbound during the mop-up, slower than the hostile wave but otherwise indistinguishable, and it never resolves. Reaches the 5 km limit near T+270 unengaged, which is the correct outcome.

success_criteria.statement: Pass requires: all three fast closers engaged at the earliest valid firing solution the system offers and destroyed; the unmanned wave then worked as a continuous queue on next-available-valid-solution, with no more than two unmanned hostiles reaching the 5 km inner limit unserviced; every Unknown track referred to the commander; and no round fired at any track not classified Enemy. Engaging an Unknown or a friendly is an outright fail regardless of hostiles destroyed. A leaked fast closer fails the run. Holding fire while both rockets are committed is correct behaviour, not inaction — breaking or retargeting a committed engagement is scored as an error even if the outcome is favourable. No more than thirteen interceptors may be expended out of the sixteen held.

revisions.request: The window is far too long and nothing happens for the first two minutes. Bring the arrivals forward.
revisions.notes: Cut the window from 315 s to 195 s (brief now matches at 195, not the stale 210) and pulled every arrival forward: the three fast closers now present valid long-range solutions at roughly T+16, T+29 and T+47 instead of T+21/43/58 with a 20 s spawn delay, and the unmanned wave now enters between T+15 and T+92 at 13–26 km rather than T+25–118 at 10–30 km, so all seven reach the 5 km inner limit between T+157 and T+193 — inside the run rather than after it. Unknown resolution times moved forward in step (helicopter T+110, friendly UAV T+150) and the jet spawn ranges/track notes were corrected so the stated ring-crossing times are arithmetically true; composition, bearings, classes, IFF truth and success criteria are untouched.

revisions.request:
add unknown targets with IFF mode 3 that the trainee shouldn't classify as an enemy and shouldn't kill.
give some of the enemy targets IFF mode 1.
make sure the trainee have enough ammunition to kill all the enemy forces.
revisions.notes: Two things in your second list I could not do as asked and did the nearest legal thing instead: the system profile declares all three track classes (Jet, Helicopter, UAV) as carrying no transponder and has IFF interrogation disabled, so no Mode 3 or Mode 1 code can be written on any track without breaking the profile — instead I added two further must-not-engage tracks that enter Unknown (TN-4213, a high fast crosser that never resolves, and TN-4214, a friendly UAV in the middle of the mop-up that also never resolves), and left every hostile system-classified Enemy from first detection so the enemy set is positively distinguishable, which is the closest analogue to your Mode 1 request. On the clock: 315 s is the hard floor for a 70 km envelope with a 600-kt jet, so I could not shorten it; instead I pulled every arrival forward (all fifteen tracks are up by T+50 instead of T+92), moved the jets in so they cross the long ring at T+15/T+30/T+45, and tightened the UAV spawns so their 5 km deadlines all fall between T+154 and T+177 — the run is now decided inside the first three minutes and the last stretch is outcome. Ammunition raised to 16 rounds held (5 long / 6 medium / 5 short) with the spend cap lifted from 11 to 13, i.e. one per hostile plus three spares, and the brief's stale '195 seconds' corrected to 315.
